title: Ankara / Istanbul
hook: 1300 → 1530. Two fixed dots; compare the reconstruction's labels.

knows: two points can be located on a map
doesNotKnow: how this reconstruction classifies Ankara / Istanbul in 1300 and 1530, and what that comparison cannot establish

misconception: A historical map's region labels directly establish exact borders, continuous control and the history of everyone inside.
objective: Compare the source's labels at two fixed points in 1300 and 1530; distinguish the observed map pattern from claims about its cause or legitimacy.

claims.text: Ankara area anchor: 32.86, 39.93 (0 km from the nominal location); Istanbul area anchor: 28.905035, 41.066569 (8.9 km from the nominal location). Modern place names orient the fixed comparison points, not historical settlement names or exact city centres.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/cases.mjs: nominal WGS84 longitude/latitude points; generate.mjs areaAnchor prefers the nearest point covered by both snapshots within 75 km, without selecting for an answer. map.json records nominal and actual coordinates and the offset. A place name is not an ancient-settlement claim.

claims.text: The 1300 and 1530 stages are clipped Mercator paths from these GeoJSON snapshots, with all matched NAME labels retained: [[["Seljuk Caliphate"],["Byzantine Empire"]],[["Ottoman Empire"],["Ottoman Empire"]]]. Map key and SVG titles use these labels; NAME is not SUBJECTO.
claims.source: Ring directions normalised for d3 spherical exteriors/holes; coordinates and feature order retained. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1300.geojson (SHA-256 a27985e60d936611d7933f0c30f1b52c36ef4a17225dfac25fb96abe40fa496f); GeoJSON features [[97],[144]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1530.geojson (SHA-256 984005809f085285a48318600e3a198274eb4679f5360ebfaead29da496e9f5b); GeoJSON features [[493],[405]]

claims.text: At the two points, 1300 has different labels and 1530 has same label. This supports the prediction answer and first reveal sentence.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/generate.mjs: geoContains on every feature; sorted unique NAME sets, exact set equality; missing sets stay unlabelled. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1300.geojson (SHA-256 a27985e60d936611d7933f0c30f1b52c36ef4a17225dfac25fb96abe40fa496f); GeoJSON features [[97],[144]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1530.geojson (SHA-256 984005809f085285a48318600e3a198274eb4679f5360ebfaead29da496e9f5b); GeoJSON features [[493],[405]]

claims.text: The maps are approximate reconstructions. Two snapshots do not date a transition, establish continuity, explain causes, or settle present-day claims; an unlabelled dot does not prove empty land.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md, sections Conceptual limitations and disputed territories / Polygons; two-endpoint inference limit. Stage caption, reveal, hook 'reconstruction', and prediction wording are covered here. Cultural and research reviews remain required.

claims.text: Two territories have different local labels. Could the source group both under one ruling power? Answer: Yes; label and ruling-power fields can differ The source distinguishes NAME from SUBJECTO. This exercise compares NAME only; it does not count sovereign states.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md (source limitations); tools/history-maps/generate.mjs recalls[4]. Interpret the dataset fields and projection, not historical causes.

recall.question: Two territories have different local labels. Could the source group both under one ruling power?
options: Yes; label and ruling-power fields can differ
Only if their borders are straight
recall.why: The source distinguishes NAME from SUBJECTO. This exercise compares NAME only; it does not count sovereign states.

careLine: Source NAME labels are classifications, not statements of legitimate sovereignty, ethnicity, religion, language or absence of people. Modern place names are orientation aids only. Retain missing coverage and overlapping labels.
